title: The Letters of Ghalib (Khutoot-e-Ghalib; compiled as Urdu-e-Mu'alla)
published_date: 1869 (compiled in his lifetime; later scholarly editions)

access.edition_or_version: The Oxford India Ghalib: Life, Letters, and Ghazals, trans. Ralph Russell and Khurshidul Islam (OUP, 2003)

mechanics.tone_relevance: Non-Anglophone anchor for addressed intimate disclosure: Ghalib made letter-writing conversational ('murasale ko mukalima bana diya'), dissolving the formal Persianate frame.
mechanics.point_of_view: First person, addressed to named disciples and friends; each letter constructs a specific intimate dyad.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Varies by correspondent; after 1857 the letters disclose grief, loss, and the destruction of Delhi to trusted recipients.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Informal salutation, conversational diction, ironic self-deprecation, abrupt shifts between banter and lament.
mechanics.dialogue: The letter is written as a conversation, anticipating and answering the recipient rather than reporting to a stranger.
mechanics.register: Colloquial Urdu against a courtly Persianate convention; the downward register shift signals intimacy.
mechanics.intimacy_technique: Address to a real reader plus a lowered register and shared shorthand produce closeness without formal exposure.
mechanics.translation_note: Nastaliq Urdu into English loses syntactic and idiomatic weight; register fidelity varies by translation.
mechanics.copyright_note: Original Urdu/Persian letters public domain; translations copyrighted. Techniques described, no text reproduced.
